1.OBJECTIVES 
 
1-1- The objective of this policy is to maintain a 
healthy, convenient, and unique work 
environment always by setting the rules, 
and regulations for people behavior inside 
the company’s head office.   
 
2.SCOPE 
 
2-1- All employees who work at Rowad Modern 
Engineering’s head office. 
 
2-2- All visitors, service providers, and job 
applicants at Rowad Modern Engineering.

3.POLICY DETAILS: 
 
3-1- Administrative Head Office: 
3-1-1- Non-Smoking Office Policy: 
 3-1-1-1- It’s only allowed to smoke in the 
designated areas outside the building. 
 
3-1-1-2- It’s totally prohibited to smoke (all 
forms of smoking) inside the building, with no 
exceptions, as the building is equipped with 
smoke detectors that will activate the fire alarm 
in case of sensing any smoke. 
 
 3-1-1-3- It’s also prohibited to smoke in front of 
the building entrance as it affects our image. 
 
3-1-2- Dining Policy: 
3-1-2-1- Dining is allowed in the designated 
areas, mainly the ground floor cafeteria and the 
shaded seating areas outside the building. 
 
3-1-2-2- Eating in the offices areas is not 
allowed,  for maintaining cleanliness, to avoid 
strong odors and conserve the company image. 
 
3-1-2-3- The duration to use the cafeteria is 20 
minutes only to allow access for all colleagues.

3-1-2-4- Each employee is required to clear any 
food receipts on daily basis through the 
cafeteria. 
3-1-2-5- Food brought to the office should 
be always kept in fridges availed in each 
floor. No food should be kept in the drawer 
set. 
 
3-1-3- Ordering and drinking beverages: 
3-1-3-1- The company will pay a fixed monthly 
beverages allowance for all employees working 
in the Head Office. 
 
3-1-3-2- It’s allowed to have beverages in the 
office work areas, while maintaining cleanliness 
and furniture tidiness. 
 
3-1-3-3 Beverages are available through the 
cafeteria only. 
 
3-1-3-4- Kettles and coffee makers are not 
allowed for use in the office’s areas. 
 
3-1-3-5- Staff to cover beverages expenses 
utilized in the cafeteria by deduction from 
monthly pay. 
 
3-1-3-6- All employees are required to use their 
own glasses for drinking water, to prevent the 
impact on environment. 
 
3-1-3-7- The company covers the guests’ 
delivered beverages against signed receipts 
from hosting employee.  
 
3-1-3-8- Department Manager to sign 
consolidated monthly charges to release 
payments utilized by their department. 
 
3-1-4- The Building Main Gate:  
3-1-4-1- Accessing and exiting the building is 
only allowed through the main gate, except for 
managers who can access the basement’s 
parking area. 
 
3-1-4-2- Recording the fingerprint check-in and 
out is through the assigned devices installed at 
the main entrance.

3-1-4-3- Waiting by the main entrance for the 
purpose of drinking and/or smoking is not 
allowed to maintain the good impression. It is 
only allowed at the designated shaded areas. 
 
3-1-4-4- Reception area at each floor represents 
our image. Everyone is responsible for using a 
calm tone and avoiding conversations at this 
area. 
 
3-1-4-5- Please follow Security and HSE 
instructions while using the elevators. 
 
 
3-1-5- Building Garage: 
3-1-5-1- The parking areas in the basement are 
assigned for managers who are allowed to use 
the garage as well as cars serving the Head 
Office. 
 
3-1-5-2- Other staff can use external parking 
outside building. 
 
3-1-5-3- All staff are required to maintain curtesy 
by avoiding: 
-Double parking 
-Occupying more than 1 parking slot by their 
car, or parking the car in any non-parking 
space. 
 
3-1-6- Employees’ Offices: 
The open office areas are designed to serve our 
day-to-day business purpose. To keep it at its 
best condition, everyone is required to avoid the 
following: 
3-1-6-1- Moving any office or drawer unit 
without referring to the Facility Management 
department. 
 
3-1-6-2-  Any changes in the seating plan must 
be approved by the Admin department. 
 
3-1-6-3- Leaving any personal valuable item 
unattended in any public area. It is full 
responsibility of its owner.

3-1-6-4- Sitting and/or writing on the desks is 
forbidden. Everyone should use the furniture for 
its designated purpose. 
3-1-6-5-The hot desking area is dedicated for 
projects manager. 
 
3-1-7- What is required from Everyone:  
3-1-7-1-  Everyone is responsible for always 
maintaining a clean and tidy desk. 
 
3-1-7-2- By the end of every working day, the 
desk must be cleared of any paperwork that 
may be lost or damaged during the daily 
cleaning works. 
 
3-1-7-3- After finishing the working day, it is 
necessary to switch off your PC/Laptop, drawer 
units, and remove any paper on printer to 
maintain the confidentiality of company’s 
information. 
 
3-1-7-4- It’s prohibited to hang any frames, or 
drawings to maintain the unified design, with no 
exceptions. 
 
 
3-1-7-5- The central AC temperature is 
programmed at 25 degrees Celsius, to suit the 
majority, and it is not permitted to change it in 
open office areas. 
 
3-1-7-6- It’s not allowed to receive personal 
visits to the building as the workplace is for 
work purpose only. 
 
3-1-7-7- In the case of urgent need to work after 
six pm, the Facility Management department 
should be notified. 
 
3-1-7-8- Elevators are available for use. We also 
encourage using the stairs if accessing a near 
floor.  
 
3-1-7-9- Emergency doors are assigned for 
emergency exits only and in cases of building 
evacuation. Everyone should be careful not to 
use in normal conditions.

3-1-7-10- For reporting any emergency, the 
control room must be notified using the internal 
telephone. 
 
3-1-7-11- In the event of expecting a guest or a 
visitor for a work-related matter, it is necessary 
to contact the reception desk at Main Entrance 
to leave their name and to where they should be 
directed. 
 
3-1-7-12- Representatives of banks, insurance 
companies, and service providers are 
welcomed at the reception area. They are not 
allowed to access other floors inside the 
building. 
 
3-1-7-13- Mobile phones should be set on a 
mode suitable for the work environment in 
terms of ringing tone and volume and using it 
in a calm manner to avoid distracting others. 
 
 
3-1-8- Meeting & Training Rooms: 
3-1-8-1- Business meeting rooms are in each 
floor and can be booked through the floor’s 
reception desk. 
 
3-1-8-2- It’s prohibited to eat in any business 
meeting rooms. 
 
3-1-8-3- It can be used only to conduct 
business meetings. 
 
3-1-8-4- Other colleagues from projects who 
are assigned to temporary works in Head 
Office should seek receptionist’s guidance 
to facilitate using a meeting room. 
 
3-1-9- Toilets: 
3-1-9-1- Water supply in toilets is not suitable for 
drinking, it is suitable for ablution and external 
use. 
The following must be considered regarding 
maintaining the toilets: 
3-1-9-2- Notify the responsible housekeeping 
supervisor of any  cleanliness note.   
 
3-1-9-3- Keep and leave the toilet clean.

1. Objectives 
To facilitate the move to the administrative headquarters 
in New Cairo for Rowad’s employees. 
The company decided to stipulate with a provider 
specialized in transportation services. Company to 
provide air-conditioned buses according to the enclosed 
transportation lines, for those who wish to use, at a partial 
rate from the company within the limits of 50%, and the 
employees to bear a cost of around EGP 650 per month. 
This is according to current prices, with the possibility of 
future adjustment in the event of changes to fuel cost.

All Rowad Modern Engineering employees in the head

implicitly indicates employee’s acknowledgment and 
compliance with all the terms in this policy. 
2. Administration shall appoint 2 supervisors from the 
passengers of each bus to communicate in the case 
of delays from the service provider. 
3. Service is based on meeting points on the main 
roads, after a research and a study of the 
transportation lines and stop-points in line with the 
numbers of beneficiaries and timings of attendance 
and departure and will be reviewed periodically. 
4. It is necessary to ensure that the timing 
(hours/minutes) is consistent between the 
employees and the driver to avoid any differences in 
timing.

4. Administration Rules & General Behavior: 
 
1. It is not allowed to play any multimedia on personal 
mobiles unless through headsets. 
2. AC temperature inside the bus is set to accommodate 
everyone and cannot be changed by passengers. 
3. Seats inside the bus cannot be pre-reserved by 
anyone. The first-come first-serve is the primary rule in 
all cases. 
4. Committing to one seat is a must and not putting bags 
or laptop cases or any other personal belongings on 
the seat designated for other colleagues.   
5. Colleagues are required to be present at the meeting 
points at the specified times without delay. It is not the 
authority of any passenger to instruct the driver to wait 
after the specified departure time. 
6. Colleagues are required to board the bus immediately 
after the end of each working day, for the return trip to 
start at the specified time, which is exactly 05:15 pm. 
7. It is not allowed to speak to the driver except when 
necessary, for example, if he fails to comply with traffic 
rules, and it is the responsibility of one of the bus 
supervisors assigned by administration.

1. OBJECTIVES 
1-1- Rowad recognizes that different 
perspectives and inclusive thinking are key 
drivers of innovation, and diversity and that 
equality and inclusion are essential in the 
development of creative solutions. 
1-2- Encouraging equality, diversity, and 
inclusion among our workforce, and to 
eliminate discrimination which will have a 
positive impact on our workforce as 
individuals, but also allows for sustainable 
economic and social growth, and healthy 
competition. 
1-3- To ensure that our workforce truly represents 
all sections of society, & that no one is 
treated unfairly, inappropriately, or 
disrespectfully, and that each employee 
feels respected, able to give their best at our 
workplace, and empowered to thrive and 
succeed 
1-4- Diversity, equality, and inclusion for the 
purposes of this policy, refer to the creation 
of a respectful work environment with equal 
rights, responsibilities and opportunities in 
which people neither discriminate nor are 
discriminated against any context on the 
basis of the following characteristics: 
1. Age  
2. Ethnicity 
3. Race 
4. Religion 
5. Physical Ability/Disability 
6. Gender  
7. Marital Status 
8. Family Status (including pregnancy, 
maternity, paternity status)  
9. Socioeconomic Background

3. PROCESS OPERATIONS 
Diversity, Equality, & Inclusion Policy Details : 
 
This policy is an internal guidance document, 
outlining strategic priorities and processes for 
integrating gender perspectives across the 
company.
This policy sets out our approach to inclusion and 
diversity and the avoidance of discrimination at 
work aiming at the following:
• Remove obstacles to equal enjoyment of 
people’s rights at work, and adopt protection 
measures and apply the grievance mechanism 
including positive measures in all areas as a 
supportive work environment for people, to 
achieve equal empowerment for all segments. 
• Promote a gender-aware and gender-
responsive culture throughout the organization, 
that values and integrates gender 
considerations in each aspect of the workplace. 
• Overcome barriers to gender equality in the 
workplace, including gender biases and 
stereotyping. 
• Ensure that all employees have an 
understanding of gender issues and the 
objectives of this policy.

6. Our Disciplinary & Grievance Procedures 
According to Rowad Modern Engineering C.A.R.E 
process (Complain, Action & Review Process). It 
is responsibility of Human Resource Manager to 
facilitate and manage the process and therefore, 
the manager of Human Resource may be 
involved in this process at any step. It works as 
follows: 
• Step 1: Employee will discuss the matter 
informally with his direct manager. 
• Step 2: If Step 1 doesn’t solve the problem, 
employee will fill a written complaint with 
Human Resource Office within 14 days after 
the event or problem occurrence. Human 
Resource Manager may at his/her request 
assist him\her in preparing the complaint. 
• Step 3: Human Resources Manager will 
conduct an investigation and a hearing 
concerning the employee’s written complaint 
within 7 days after filing. 
• Step 4: Human Resources Manager will issue 
a written decision to the employee within 7 
days after closing of the investigation and 
hearing.

5. Procedures 
5.1. 
Hiring Casual Labor 
Refer to Wages & Hiring for Casual Labor Process “P-
HR-06”) 
5.1.1. Casual Labor Department shall study all 
categories of professions in each region and 
adopt quarterly values to be used as a 
reference for determining wages and share 
them with Projects Control and Tendering 
Departments for guidance during pricing. 
5.1.2. For projects in remote areas, a project 
allowance is added after reviewing the project 
budget by the Projects Control department and 
the amount shall be set in agreement with the 
COO and Human Resources department. 
5.1.3. The indirect Labors do not have any 
discretionary bonuses calculated except upon 
the approval of both the Chief Operations 
Officer and the Human Resources Department, 
based on job requirements. 
5.1.4. The maximum actual additional hours for 
indirect Labors are 4 hours per day, and they 
shall not exceed this limit except with the 
approval of both the Operations Manager and

1. Objective 
1.1. We believe that the keystone to our business’ 
success is integrity with respect to our dealings 
with clients, suppliers, and governments. The 
highest order of ethical conduct has and will be 
the very foundation of our enterprise. These 
qualities have been instilled and transmitted 
throughout the company. 
1.2. This code of conduct provides firm and 
uncompromising standards for each of us in 
our dealings with our agents, clients, suppliers, 
political entities, and others. 
1.3. The code re-emphasizes and provides further 
guidance regarding policies which are an 
integral part of Rowad business philosophy. 
1.4. Adherence to the code is the responsibility of 
each employee of Rowad and its subsidiaries 
and a condition of continued employment. It 
will be administered uniformly throughout the 
company and independent of the practices of 
other companies. Adherence to the code will 
continue to be the subject of management’s 
attention.

work for a political candidate or party or used the 
company’s funds to reimburse employees for 
political contributions made with their private 
funds. 
 
5.2. Clients\Suppliers\Government Relationships: 
 
• Information disclosed by a client to an employee, 
clearly identified verbally or in writing as sensitive, 
private, or confidential, shall be protected from 
disclosure to unauthorized persons inside and 
outside the company to the same extent as the 
company's sensitive, private or confidential 
information is protected, except where such 
information was already known to company or 
was made public.  
Example: The company's price and quotation to a 
customer will not be disclosed to employees 
without the need to know and never outside the 
company unless is required to be released by law 
or regulation.

5.3. Selection of Suppliers and Service Providers:  
 
5.3.1. Rowad conducts fair and unbiased 
examinations of all offers submitted by its 
suppliers. The assessment, awarding and 
handling of a contract must be based on 
strictly professional criteria and be carried out 
in a transparent manner. It is not allowed 
under any circumstances to give undue 
preference to a supplier or impede its efforts 
to win a contract. When selecting business 
partners, we demand that they too respect the 
values set forth in this Code. Infringement by a 
partner can lead to termination of the 
business relationship.  
Refer to the Vendor Selection and Bidding 
Process (P-VMO-01). 
Example: Suppliers win Rowad, and its affiliates 
business based on product or service suitability, 
price, delivery, and quality. There is no other basis. 
Attempts to influence procurement decisions by 
offers of any compensation, commission, 
kickbacks, paid vacation, and special discount on 
product service, entertainment or any other form of 
gift or gratuity must be firmly rejected by all 
employees and will be severely punished in case of 
proof of such misconduct. 
5.3.2. Employees of Rowad shall respect the law, 
customs, and traditions of the country in 
which they operate and will at the same time, 
engage in no act or course of conduct, which 
even if legal, customary and accepted in any 
such country, could be deemed to be in 
violation of the accepted business ethics of 
Rowad and the laws of country's relating to 
business ethics. 
5.3.3. Employees of Rowad shall not accept any 
payments, gifts or gratuities of any kind 
(including any favors which might be regarded 
as placing the employees under some 
obligation to a third party dealing or desiring 
to deal with Rowad). However, in rare 
circumstances, where the refusal to accept a 
gift or gratuity may be impossible without 
injuring the legitimate business interest of 
Rowad, such gifts may be accepted if their 
amount is within the limit of $50 or its 
equivalent in Egyptian Pounds.

5.4. Conflict of Interest: 
The interest of Rowad employees associated with a 
supplier, client or competitor may create a conflict 
of interest depending on the facts and 
circumstances of the case. 
Conflict of interest for purpose of this policy 
statement may result if one of the following 
situations occurred: 
• 
The existence of any family relationship to an 
employee of Modern Engineering Company, or 
the presence of any member of the employee’s 
family or those who support them, or who 
provides them with financial support in any way 
or has a personal relationship with them. 
• 
The existence of a work relationship in which the 
employee benefits from a financial interest, 
whether there are any financial dues owed by 
the employee to external parties, in which it is 
expected to reduce the obligations owed by the 
employee or achieve any personal gains or 
advantages. 
 
5.5. Avoidance of Conflicts: 
 
 It is important to Rowad that their employees do not 
have a conflict of interest or disloyalty in the course 
of their work. Such conflict can occur if, for example, 
there are business transactions between Rowad 
and employees or members of their families. If such 
occurs, the transaction must be disclosed in 
advance to the employee's superior. 
 
 
5.6. Employment by Third Party: 
 
Rowad employees shall not: 
 
• 
Be employed by any other firm or person, 
including self-employment, if such firm or 
person is a competitor or supplier of Rowad.  
• 
Engage in any activity where his/her personal 
skills and knowledge develop or applies in the 
employer's position is transferred or applied to 
such activity in derogation of the present or 
prospective business interests of Rowad. 
• 
Rowad employees shall not have any 
relationship with any other business enterprise

5.7.4. Leadership & Employees at Rowad: 
Productivity and humanity must go hand in hand to 
ensure sustained success in an enterprise. Rowad 
economic success is dependent on the help and 
cooperation of its employees. 
 
5.7.5. Leadership & Trust: 
All our employees are required to adhere to the 
code, and our management personnel must set an 
example. Rowad cultivates an atmosphere of trust 
in which its managers are responsible for providing 
sufficient supervision to prevent any violations of 
the code.  
 
5.7.6. Tolerance & Equal Opportunities: 
 
• 
Rowad respects basic human rights. We work 
with male and female employees and business 
partners who have different cultures and 
customs, and we do not tolerate any kind of 
discrimination or unlawful treatment 
(discrimination), belittlement, or degradation. 
• 
Specifically, Rowad does not tolerate 
discrimination on account of race, ethnic origin, 
gender, religion or worldview, political opinions, 
age or gender identity. 
 
5.7.7. Fair Working Conditions: 
 
Rowad provides its employees with adequate 
wages and fair working conditions that meet all 
legal requirements. We reject every form of forced 
labor and underage work, and legal representation 
will not hinder the interests of the workers. 
 
5.7.8. Safeguarding of Assets:  
Rowad asks its employees to protect the 
company's tangible and intangible assets. These 
assets include real estate, production equipment, 
warehouse contents, cash flow, office equipment 
and supplies, information systems and programs, 
as well as patents, commercial property rights, and 
technical know-how. Fraud, theft, embezzlement,

5.7.9. Use of information: 
We expect employees to take appropriate care 
when using the company’s information. 
 
 
5.7.10. Confidentiality: 
Confidentiality must be maintained concerning in-
house matters that have not been disclosed to the 
public. This also applies to inventions and other 
kinds of know-how. These are essential to the long-
term success of Rowad. Employees must therefore 
not pass information about company secrets in any 
form to third parties. This also applies after 
termination of employment. 
 
5.7.11. Privacy and Information Security: 
The global electronic exchange of information is 
essential for effective work and business success in 
general. But besides having benefits, electronic 
communication can pose risks to privacy and data 
protection. Official documents and data storage 
media must therefore always be protected from 
access by third parties. Both managers and 
employees must take effective protective measures 
against these risks, and this is an important 
component of IT management. 
5.7.12. Insider Knowledge: 
It is not permissible to derive personal advantages 
or advantages for others using in-house 
knowledge. The same applies to unauthorized 
disclosure of such knowledge.

When making oral or written reports for in-house or

5.8. Implementation of the Code of Conduct: 
All Rowad employees are required to apply this 
policy effective from its date of issuance and any 
violation shall be recorded via the Employee 
Misconduct Record (F-M-HR-10-02).

• 
Any employee can and has the right to report a 
violation or suspected violation of the code of 
conduct to the management by sending an e-
mail to grievance@rowad-rme.com or file a 
written complaint using Complaint Form (F-
M-HR-13-01) to the Human Resources 
Office. 
• 
An employee who, based on tangible evidence, 
honestly believes that the code of conduct has 
been or might have been violated and who 
makes use of the right to report this to the 
management will not suffer any kind of 
retaliation. In such case, necessary steps will be 
taken to protect the employee against such 
retaliate, to the extent possible and legally 
permissible, the management will maintain 
confidentiality about the identity of any 
employee who follows this procedure to report a 
violation or suspected violation of the code of 
conduct. The same applies to the identity of 
employees who cooperate in the investigation 
of such violations or suspected violations.

or Lost Time Incident (LTI).

adequately be treated by a nurse or a first 
aider. 
4.6. Near Miss: An unplanned event with High 
Potential (HIPO) to cause a serious injury 
but did not result in any injury. This does not 
include unsafe conditions where no 
uncontrolled events have occurred.

requires an extinguishing media to put it out

French-Speaking Sub-Saharan Africa Policy
 
Politique de l’Afrique subsaharienne francophone
 
Effective Date: April, 2025
 
Rev. No.: 01
 
Doc. No.: M-HR-12
 
 
Page 1 of 4
 
1. OBJECTIVES 
The objective of this policy is to set the workflow 
for projects at French-speaking Sub-Saharan 
Africa. 
2. SCOPE 
All employees who are assigned on projects at 
French-speaking Sub-Saharan Africa. 
 
1. OBJECTIFS 
L'objectif de cette politique est de définir le flux 
de travail des projets en Afrique subsaharienne 
francophone. 
2. CHAMP D'APPLICATION 
Tous les employés affectés aux projets en 
Afrique subsaharienne francophone. 
3. POLICY OPERATIONS 
3.1. 
Pay Policy: 
3.1.1. A pay methodology is issued for projects 
at French-speaking Sub-Saharan Africa to 
consider the context and the budget 
issued by Tendering department for each 
project.  
 
3.1.2. Job offers for expat shall be in Euro & 
salary shall be paid equivalent to FCFA. In 
cases where the client contract is issued 
in a different currency, top management 
shall determine the currency to be used 
for the job offer. 
 
3.2. Contracts: (All staff deployed at French-
speaking Sub-Saharan Africa projects will 
sign a contract including the following 
terms) 
3.2.1. Duration: Project duration 
3.2.2. Working hours: 8 hours per day excluding 
the break. Extra working hours may be 
required in some project phases 
according to business need. Local 
country rules will apply as per local labour 
law for direct manpower only. 
 
 
 
3.2.3. Transferred Egyptian Staff’s Egyptian 
Social Insurance charges for the duration 
of deployment will be incurred by Rowad. 
 
 
3. OPÉRATIONS DE POLITIQUE 
3.1. 
Politique Salariale : 
3.1.1. Une méthodologie de rémunération est 
émise pour les projets en Afrique 
subsaharienne francophone afin de tenir 
compte du contexte et du budget émis 
par le service des appels d'offres pour 
chaque projet.  
3.1.2. Les offres d'emploi pour les expatriés 
doivent être libellées en euros et le 
salaire doit être équivalent en francs 
CFA. Si le contrat client est établi dans 
une autre devise, la direction 
déterminera la devise à utiliser pour 
l'offre d'emploi. 
 
3.2. 
Contrats: (Tout le personnel affecté sur 
les projets en Afrique subsaharienne 
francophone signera un contrat 
comprenant les conditions suivantes)  
 
3.2.1. Durée : Délai d’exécution du projet  
3.2.2. Horaires de travail : 8 heures par jour 
exclus les heures de pose. Des heures 
de travail supplémentaires peuvent être 
nécessaires dans certaines phases du 
projet selon les besoins de l'entreprise. 
Les règles locales du pays 
s'appliqueront conformément au code 
du travail local pour la main d'oeuvre 
directe uniquement. 
3.2.3. Les frais d’assurance sociale du 
personnel égyptien transféré pour la 
durée du déploiement seront à la 
charge de Rowad.

3.3. 
Rotation et billets d’avion :  
3.3.1. Se référer à l'Annexe 1.

pendant la période de rotation.  
3.3.3. Les jours consommés au-delà des jours 
de rotation autorisés seront considérés 
comme un congé non payé. 
 
3.4. 
Politique de congé et jours fériés :  
 
3.4.1. Conformément au code du travail local.

Politique d’hébergement :  
Selon les catégories mentionnées à l’Annexe 1 
dans les conditions suivantes :  
3.5.1. Frais de fonctionnement des 
appartements à la charge de Rowad. 
3.5.2. Le Housekeeping sera fourni par 
Rowad.  
3.5.3. Tous les frais supplémentaires 
découlant d'un abus de ressources 
seront à la charge des occupants. 
 
3.6. 
Services Médicaux:  
3.6.1. Le personnel égyptien de Rowad 
s’engage à effectuer les contrôles 
médicaux requis et à recevoir les 
vaccins requis avant le voyage. Tous les 
frais de vaccination en plus de la 
délivrance du certificat jaune seront 
couverts par Rowad.  
3.6.2. Jusqu'à ce que le contrat d'assurance 
médicale soit émis, les frais médicaux 
seront supportés par le budget du projet 
de Rowad. Le personnel demandant un 
remboursement médical doit présenter 
une ordonnance du médecin ainsi que 
les reçus du traitement recommandé.  
3.6.3. Nouveau personnel nommé directement 
sur des projets en Afrique 
subsaharienne francophone, Rowad 
couvrira les frais d'assurance sociale et 
médicale au Caire.  
3.6.4. Les frais d’assurance sociale et

à des projets en Afrique subsaharienne 
francophone et transféré d’Égypte 
seront déduits du salaire de l’employé

4. Terms & Definitions 
Promotion: Transfer to a higher position, grade, 
level of responsibility and salary. As an original 
principle, promotion is related to performance, 
competencies, and the ability to grow within the 
organization, as well as the company’s 
business needs.  
Fast-tracked: Employees who are identified as 
High Potential/ Key Talent and are accelerated 
on the relevant ladder. 
Dual Career Ladder: Different routes or paths 
based on the potential future roles. 
Job Family: A group of jobs with similar nature, 
characteristics, and career paths. 
Leader Ladder: A career path that includes 
leadership jobs and people management 
responsibilities. 
Career Path: A career path constitutes the steps 
upon which an employee progresses vertically, 
Laterally, or diagonally in his/her career. 
Assessment:  Assessment Tools (Centers, 
Cognitive Tests, Behavioral Tests… etc.). 
Tenure: Length of service. 
Middle Management: Employees responsible 
for supervising teams and implementing 
organizational strategies, typically including 
Team Leaders, Section Heads.

5. Policy Details: 
5.1. General Principles: 
5.1.1. Rowad is entitled to provide equal 
opportunities for employees to pursue a 
successful career. 
5.1.2. Promotional decisions are made based 
on objective measurement tools that 
consider business needs, different 
employment parameters, and 
contributions made by an employee. 
5.1.3. Promotional decisions follow a 
structured approval cycle that ensures 
equity and eliminates nepotism, 
misconduct, favoritism, discrimination or 
conflict of interest. 
5.1.4. Transfers within the same level and 
grade are not considered a promotional 
move and are not addressed by this 
policy. 
5.1.5. If a position becomes unexpectedly 
vacant and the company decides to fill it 
internally, an employee may be 
temporarily assigned to the role until the 
next promotion cycle. 
5.1.6. High-potential employees are those who 
consistently exceed their objectives and 
demonstrate outstanding behavior and 
competencies.  
5.1.7. To be eligible for promotion, employees 
must meet the following criteria: 
• 
Have a minimum of one year of service 
with the company, with no warnings or 
disciplinary actions on record. 
• 
Obtain a recommendation from the 
direct manager. 
• 
Ensure there is an available position 
within the organizational structure. 
• 
Successfully complete the performance 
assessment tests and secure eligible 
positioning within the nine-box grid. 
5.1.8. The promotion can’t be two grades 
movement within the same function. 
5.1.9. Employees who are on unpaid leave for 
more than 3 months during the previous 
two consecutive years are not eligible 
for promotion.

5.2. Promotional Movements: 
5.2.1. Promotional moves shall be just one 
level or grade up from the current role. 
5.2.2. Promotional moves occur when an 
employee’s grade and level change due 
to: 
Vertical Move: A change in which an employee 
advances to a higher-level role within the same 
function and department, driven by hierarchical 
needs, role enrichment, and/or demonstrated 
expertise. This type of promotion follows a 
structured path from entry-level to the highest 
position within the same functional area. 
Diagonal Move: A change where an employee 
moves to a higher-level role in a different 
function & department which is accompanied 
by a change in scope and role. Employees are 
eligible for a Diagonal Move if they meet the 
following conditions: 
1. Must have achieved a minimum of "Exceeds 
Expectations" in the last two consecutive 
performance cycles. 
2. Must be positioned in (High Performance – 
High Potential) of the 9-Box Grid. Refer to 
Annex 5. 
3. Must demonstrate competencies required 
for the target role, as validated through a 
competency-based assessment.

5.8. 
Assessment Tools : 
5.8.1. Box Grid:   
9 box grid is a  talent management tool in which 
employees are segmented into nine groups 
based on two dimensions – performance and 
competencies/Potential . 
5.8.2. Creating a 9-box grid involves three 
steps:  
• 
Evaluating performance. 
• 
Evaluating potential. 
• 
Bringing the two dimensions together. 
5.8.3. Evaluating Performance (measured by 
KPIs): 
Low Performance: The employee does not 
match the requirements of their job and fails 
their individual targets. 
Moderate Performance: The employee partially 
matches the requirements of their job and their 
individual targets. 
High Performance: The employee fully meets 
the requirements of their job and their individual 
targets. 
5.8.4. Evaluating Potential (measured by 
competency evaluations, leadership 
assessments, learning agility, and 
adaptability): 
Low potential | Working at Full Potential: The 
employee is working at full potential and is not 
expected to improve, either because they are at 
maximum capacity or because of a lack of 
motivation. 
Moderate Potential | Develop in Current Role: 
The employee has the potential to further 
develop within their current role. This can be in 
terms of performance but also in terms of 
expertise.

maternity leave for the six weeks immediately

must allow the female employee to begin her 
maternity leave at least four weeks prior to the 
date of birth, as determined by a medical 
certificate authenticated by a health agency.

Employees are entitled to a paid leave of not less 
than ten days and not more than fifteen days, 
including Eid Al-Adha holiday-to perform Hajj only 
once during employment service upon completion 
of a service period not less than two years.

Employees are entitled to paid leave of 2 days, 
renewed every 2 years.

Employees are eligible for a paid leave of 5 days 
upon exceptional cases approved by the 
management & expires at the end of every 
calendar year.

Guidelines, Control of Documents & 
Communication Process (P-QD-06). 
1. Always use the email template which contains 
the appropriate signature from Rowad - KSA.

where specifically authorised by the other 
person, do not access any other person’s in-
box or other email folders nor send any email 
purporting to come from another person.

information which is time-critical, bear in mind 
that an email is not necessarily instant 
communication and consider whether it is the 
most appropriate means of communication.

provided for the purposes of our business, we 
accept that employees may occasionally want 
to use it for their own personal purposes. This 
is permitted on the condition that all the 
procedures and rules set out in this policy are 
complied with. However, if employees choose 
to make use of our facilities for personal 
correspondence, very little privacy can be 
expected because Rowad - KSA may need to 
monitor communications.

B. Special Leaves: 
1. Medical Leaves: 
Once the employee completes the probation 
period they are entitled to up to 90 days of sick 
leave per year which may be taken continuously 
or intermittently. 
Pay Structure: 
• 
First 15 days fully paid  
• 
The following 30 days half pay  
• 
The remaining 45 days are unpaid. 
2. Compassionate Leave: 
• 
In the case of the death of the wife/husband is 
entitled for a paid leave of 5 days  
• 
In the case of the death one of the employee 
parent, child, sibling, grandchild or 
grandparent, the employee is entitled for a 
paid leave of 3 days. 
3. Marriage Leave: 
Employees are entitled to paid leave of 5 days. 
4. Paternity Leave: 
Employees are entitled to paid leave of 5 days. 
5. Maternity leave: 
Female employee is entitled for a paid maternity 
leave of 45 days (fully paid days), the following 15 
days will be 50% paid. And for 6 months from the 
date of the employee resuming work, she is 
entitled to 2 hours of reduced working hours either 
at the beginning or at the end of the working 
hours. 
 
C. Annual Leave: According to regulatory rules. 
• 
Employees are eligible to benefit from their 
annual vacation balance after 6 months from 
joining the company. 
• 
Employees shall clear his/her remaining 
vacation balance before the end of the first 
quarter of the following year. (Company has 
the right to mandate employees to clear their 
vacation balance). 
• 
Employees are eligible for AED 2500 to cover 
a ticket once per year in his/her contract and 
shall be issued after 6 months of his joining 
date and paid monthly as ticket allowance. 
• 
In case the vacation is cancelled by the 
company due to work needs, non-UAE 
employees are eligible for ticket compensation 
either in cash equivalent to the ticket value

Employees are responsible for submitting

If a mission exceeds (6) weeks from its

company’s local transfer approval cycle. Any

authorization, will be considered as leave 
without permission.

Business Partner & Project Manager. 
6.2.2. Mission request shall then be sent to the 
receiving HR Business Partner & Project

6.2.3. A notification shall be sent to HRBP, 
Payroll & Personnel, Accommodation & 
Timekeeping, BUM, PM, & Site 
Administrator. 
6.2.4. Each of these approvers must review 
and register their decision on HITS. If 
any party declines the request at any 
stage, the system automatically closes 
the request, and the mission is 
considered rejected.

6.2.5. Mission request shall be initiated by 
employee via HITS & approved by the 
Department Head. 
6.2.6. Mission request shall be approved by 
the receiving Department Head, and 
notifications shall be sent to the 
Personnel team & HR Manager.  
6.2.7. Each of these approvers must review 
and register their decision on HITS. If 
any party declines the request at any 
stage, the system automatically closes 
the request, and the transfer is

4.1. Rowad Modern Engineering provides car 
allowances and transportation services to 
support employees whose roles require 
business travel, site visits, or operational 
mobility. These services aim to ensure 
fairness, efficiency, and alignment with the 
company’s business needs. 
4.2. Employees must use company-provided cars 
or car allowances responsibly and primarily 
for official purposes. Any personal use must 
comply with the company’s vehicle use 
guidelines, and misuse may lead to 
disciplinary action. 
4.3. The selection of vehicles should balance 
safety, cost efficiency, and environmental 
sustainability. Employees receiving a car are 
responsible for keeping their vehicles 
properly maintained, and in safe, roadworthy 
conditions suitable for business use. 
4.4. The company reserves the right to review & 
adjust car entitlements or allowances based 
on role changes, business priorities, or 
market conditions. Employees are 
encouraged to contact the HR to identify their 
eligibility on transportation-related matters. 
4.5. Site employees who receive either a 
company-provided vehicle or a transportation 
allowance are not eligible to use any other 
transportation facilities provided by Rowad. 
This includes, but not limited to, company 
buses, shared transportation, or company 
cars.

The objective of the process is to emphasize Rowad’s commitment to the growth and 
development of its people. Our primary focus is advancing the skills, knowledge, and 
competencies of our workforce, ensuring that our employees continue to grow both 
professionally and personally to align with Rowad’s overarching vision, mission, and 
yearly strategic objectives, ensuring that employee development is both meaningful and 
impactful.

4.1 Anti- Harassment Policy details 
 
4-1-1 To create a safe workplace free of All 
different types of harassments that unfairly 
harm people by targeting personal 
characteristics such as race, color, sex, 
religion, age, gender, national origin or 
disability to all RME employees and 
stakeholders. 
  
4-1-2 Below are some forms of 
harassment that will not be tolerated, to 
maintain a healthy & safe work 
environment where our employees are 
supported and effectively perform their 
duties. 
 
4-2 Following are some forms and definitions 
of harassments that occur in multiple ways 
that shall be applied to any incident that might 
occur in future for any form of harassment, for 
example, but not limited to the following: 
4-2-1 Bullying: Undermines individual or 
group through persistent negative attacks. 
This typically irrational and unacceptable 
abuse of power or position can manifest 
itself in physical, verbal, or non-verbal forms . 
4-2-2 Stalking: Involves provocation or 
pestering an individual, in person or in writing 
or electronic formats or on the telephone 
causing them distress or grief . 
4-2-3  Religious beliefs: Unwanted and 
unacceptable behavior based on religious 
beliefs or practices that manifest themselves 
in physical, verbal, or non-verbal forms. 
4-2-4 Racial: Unwanted behavior based on 
race or national origin. It includes written or 
verbal threats or insults based on, race, 
ethnicity or skin color, abusive comments 
about racial origins, racist jokes, etc.

5. Procedures 
 
5-1- 
Once an incident takes place, the 
complainer shall send an email with the incident 
details to  safe.work.env@rowad-rme.com  
5-2- 
The complaint will be thoroughly investigated 
by a committee from the human resources and 
legal departments reporting to the HR Manager 
to start the investigation process. 
5-3- 
The harassment victim shall be invited to a 
meeting in person with the human resources 
committee. 
5-4- 
The suspect shall be invited to a meeting in 
person with the human resources committee. 
5-5- 
Ensuring that the complaint parties are 
committed to not to talk about the incident and 
whoever breaks this rule shall be submitted to 
disciplinary action. 
5-6- 
After hearing both parties the points of view 
shall be discussed by the committee for 
recommendation and appropriate action. 
5-7- 
The Policy shall be illustrated to both parties 
and the investigation shall be conducted. 
5-8- 
An interview will be conducted with 
witnesses if exist. 
5-9- 
The incident shall be documented with 
thorough details for any duplication. 
5-10- Ensure that the incident has occurred.  
5-11- In case of proofing that the complaint has

1. OBJECTIVES 
The objective of this process is to provide guidelines for all employees at Rowad Modern 
Engineering incurring business travel and hospitality expenses. All employees are required 
to comply with these guidelines to receive reimbursement for any expenses related to travel 
and hospitality.  
It serves as a guide on what expense types are, and are not, allowed while traveling or 
providing hospitality. Provide business travelers and employees with a reasonable level of 
service, convenience, and security at the optimum cost.

This guideline applies to Rowad Modern Engineering and all 
managed subsidiaries.

Except for business mandates, collective travel for leadership 
team shall be avoided, no more than three of leadership team 
are allowed to travel on the same flight. 
Managers should consider smooth workflow when several 
travelers are traveling together from the same department.

department. More than 3 people traveling together requires the

implementation of this policy.

4 
Travelers are required to always follow an agreed code of 
conduct during their trip. Misrepresenting expenses and/or 
incidents are considered gross misconduct and are grounds 
for disciplinary action.

Internal Audit Process 
Effective Date: February 2022 
Rev. No.:01 
Doc. No.: P-QD-01 
 
 
 
Page 1 of 7 
1. OBJECTIVES 
The objective of this process is to ensure that the Company's Quality Management System is 
being effectively implemented and complying with the international standard requirements of 
ISO 9001:2015. 
It also establishes the requirements for planning, preparation, conducting, reporting and follow-
up of the quality audit. 
2. STAKEHOLDER  
- 
All RME  
3. LIABLE STAKEHOLDER 
- 
Quality Assurance 
- 
LA / Auditor 
4. TERMS AND DEFINITION  
- Audit: A systematic documented and independent verification of the Quality System to 
determine whether or not the system is still in compliance with the requirement of the Quality 
Management System 
- Internal Audit: A systematic documented process for audit carried out by RME on itself  
- External Audit: An audit carried out by the customer / client (called 2nd party audit) or audit 
carried out by an accreditation body (called 3d party audit). 
- Audit Program: Set of arrangements is intended to achieve as specific audit purpose  
- within a specific time, frame 
- Audit Plan: Specifies how to conduct a particular audit. 
- Audit Report: A document that records the findings of an audit and indicates the causes, 
corrective and preventive actions needed 
- NCR: Nonconformity Report; Is the non-fulfilment of requirements. 
- QA: Quality Assurance  
- QMS: Quality Management System 
- LA: Lead Auditor: Carrying out audit as per the audit program, selecting the audit team, 
setting out the scope and criteria and preparing the audit report. 
- Auditor: Carrying out audits as per the audit program

assessment or an outcome of a workshop process.

and reduce threats to the process/project’s 
objectives. It identifies and assigns parties to take 
responsibility for each risk response. This process 
ensures each risk requiring a response has an 
“owner.” The Departments’ managers identify 
which strategy is best for each risk, and then select 
specific actions to implement that strategy. 
 
 
8 
V. Opportunities 
Check the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of 
the Quality Management System based on the 
results of analysis and evaluation with the outputs 
of management review.  
Actions taken to address opportunities shall be 
proportionate to the proportional impact on the 
conformity of products and services. 
 
 
9 
VI. 
Risk Monitoring and Control 
 
Risk monitoring and control tracks identified risks, 
monitors residual risks, and identifies new risks 
ensuring the execution of risk plans and evaluating 
their effectiveness in reducing risk.

0.1 General   
ROWAD Modern Engineering is a construction company established in Egypt in 1998. Rowad 
has been recognized as one of Egypt’s most reputable turnkey contractors through diversified 
alliances with major international contractors enabling the company to undertake 
multidisciplinary projects of high scale and complexity. Today Rowad is perceived as a key 
player in a large number of mega projects. In addition to Rowad’s well-established operations 
in Egypt, it has established new branches in KSA, Greece, Iraq, Côte d’Ivoire, Libya, and UAE. 
Rowad has also expanded its presence across Africa with successful projects in Algeria, 
Mozambique, Nigeria and the Republic of Chad, hence gaining a strong foothold across Africa 
and the Middle East.    
Rowad Modern Engineering Organization Chart is presented in Appendix (A), illustrating the Top 
Management and Department Heads.  
All over Rowad’s operations in Egypt and outside, its scope of work boasts sectors of Power 
Generation, Heavy Industries, Infrastructure, Bridges, Commercial Buildings, Hospitals, Hotels, 
Educational Facilities, etc.  
  
0.2 Quality Management Principles  
Rowad Modern Engineering adopted and utilized the benefits of Quality Management Principles 
in its daily activities. The intent of the quality Management Principles is to provide a foundation to 
continually improve the company’s performance. Subsequent sections of the QMS Manual 
provide Rowad’s commitments with the following Quality Management elements:  
• 
Customer focus.  
• 
Leadership.  
• 
Communication and the engagement of our people.  
• 
Process Approach.  
• 
Improvement.  
• 
Performance Evaluation  
• 
Risk & opportunity as well as evidence-based decision making.  
• 
Relationship management  
• 
Climate change  
  
  
  
1. Scope of the Quality Manual   
This Quality Manual specifies the requirements for the Quality Management system through 
which Rowad ensures consistent delivery of products and services that meet customer 
expectations and comply with regulatory requirements. It also highlights how Rowad effectively

applies the system, using a risk-based approach, to strengthen and continually improve its 
operations, outcomes, and reputation.  
  
This Quality Manual defines the requirements for the Quality Management System (QMS) 
implemented across our branches inside Egypt and overseas. It ensures the consistent delivery 
of products and services that comply with applicable standards while fostering continual 
improvement in operations, outcomes, and organizational reputation through effective alignment 
with ISO 9001:2015 standards.  
  
2. References  
ISO 9000:2015   
Quality Management System – Fundamentals and vocabulary 
ISO 9001:2015   
Quality Management System  
3. Acronyms, terminology, description and definition  
ROWAD Modern Engineering Company adopts the following terms and definitions within its 
Quality Management System:   
Document: Written information used to describe how an activity is done  
Record: Captured evidence of an activity that has been done  
Risk: Negative effect of uncertainty  
Opportunity: Positive effect of uncertainty  
Uncertainty: A deficiency of information related to understanding or knowledge of an event, its 
consequence, or likelihood  
Climate Change: Environmental conditions that directly affect manpower, work progress, 
materials, and equipment.  
SWOT Analysis: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats—and is a structured 
planning method that evaluates those four elements of a project or business venture.  
EPC: Engineering, procurement & construction.  
QMS: Quality Management System  
4. Context of the Organization  
4.1 The Organization & Its Context  
Rowad has determined the external and internal issues, including climate change impacts, that 
are relevant to its purpose and strategic direction and that affect its ability to achieve the intended 
results of its quality Management System.  
CEO, Quality Assurance Manager, as well as the department managers determine the external 
and internal Issues, considering issues arising from Legal, Technological, Competitive, Market, 
Cultural, Social, and Economic Environments. Whether International, Regional, or local.  
Rowad monitors and reviews information regarding these external and internal issues at least 
annually. Rowad applies SWOT analysis to systematically assess the influence of internal 
strengths and weaknesses, as well as external opportunities and threats.

4.2 Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties:  
Rowad understands the effect or potential effect on its ability to consistently provide products in 
the construction industry that meet or exceed the customer requirements as well as applicable 
statutory and regulatory requirements. The relevant interested parties are those that provide 
significant risks to organizational sustainability or consider contributors to Rowad’s success if 
their needs and expectations are not met. Appendix (C) identifies the interested parties, their 
requirements and Rowad mechanism.  
 
4.3 Scope of the Quality Management System  
Rowad’s scope of work boasts sectors of Power Generation, Heavy Industries and Infrastructure, 
Bridges, Commercial Buildings, Hospitals, Hotels, Educational Facilities, etc.  
The Scope of the Quality Management system of Rowad includes:  
• 
Proposals & Tendering  
• 
Project Planning  
• 
Procurement & Purchasing  
• 
Human Resourcing  
• 
Engineering  
• 
Operations  
Rowad carries out the check of design for minor issues, and for EPC projects, outsourcing is 
considered for design scope and Rowad team is coordinating with the service providers to ensure 
that client requirements are met.  
 
4.4 Quality Management System  
Rowad has determined the processes needed for the quality management system and their 
application throughout the organization in process map & Interactions of processes as shown in 
Appendix (B).  
To ensure effectiveness of the quality management system, Rowad determined, implemented 
and documented the following in its processes:  
• 
Inputs required and the outputs expected from each process.  
• 
Criteria & methods (including monitoring, measurements and related performance 
indicators) needed to ensure the effective operation control of these processes.  
• 
Resources needed for these processes.   
• 
Responsibilities and authorities’ matrices for each process.  
• 
Risks and action plan.  
• 
Opportunities and action plan

Rowad monitors these processes and makes changes as needed to ensure effectiveness and to 
enhance Quality management system.  
Rowad also maintains documented information to support the operation of its processes and 
retains documented information to have confidence that the processes are being carried out.  
 
5. Leadership  
5.1 Leadership & Commitment  
Rowad’s top management has demonstrated leadership and commitment with respect to the 
quality management system through the following:  
1. Accountable for the effectiveness of the Quality management system through periodic 
reviews, objectives evaluation, and resource provision.  
2. Establish quality policy and quality objectives for the quality management system and is 
compatible with the context and strategic direction of the organization.  
3. Determine the organizational processes with the quality management system requirement 
through process map & Interaction.  
4. Establish procedure for promoting the use of the process approach and risk-based 
thinking.  
5. Ensure that the resources needed for the quality management system are available, this 
is being periodically reviewed through management review meeting.  
6. Ensure that the quality management system achieves its intended results through 
management review meeting.  
7. Engage, direct and support employees to contribute to the effectiveness of the quality 
management system by providing training, conducting awareness programs and 
promoting improvement by introducing suggestion schemes, and conducting meetings.  
8. Support other relevant management roles to demonstrate their leadership as it applies to 
their areas of responsibility.  
9. Promote and demonstrate quality culture and ethical behavior  
Management Leadership and Commitment is clearly described in the process.   
5.1.1 Customer Focus  
Rowad’s top management demonstrates leadership & commitment with respect to 
customer’s focus by ensuring that:  
• 
Customer & applicable statutory and regulatory requirements are determined, 
understood and consistently met; through our quality procedure described in 
“Project Initiation” process.  
• 
Risks and opportunities that may affect product and service conformity, as well as 
the ability to enhance customer satisfaction, are identified and addressed within 
relevant company processes.

5.3 Organization Roles, Responsibilities & Authorities  
Rowad management ensures that the responsibilities and authorities for all relevant roles are 
assigned, communicated and understood within the organization through Rowad’s standard 
processes and Job descriptions. While assigning roles, responsibility and authority, top 
management has considered and ensured that:  
1. The quality management system conforms to the requirements of this International 
Standard.  
2. Processes achieve their intended output through assigned controls, with performance 
and improvement opportunities reported to top management via internal audits and 
management review meetings.  
3. The promotion of “Customer Focus” throughout the organization, through Rowad’s 
standard process of Customer Satisfaction.  
4. The Quality management system is maintained when changes to the system are planned 
and implemented through our Control of Documents & Communication Process.  
  
6. Planning  
6.1 Actions to address risks and opportunities  
Rowad considers the Organization and its context, the Organization’s needs and expectations, 
as well as the Risk and Opportunities in its Quality Management System, QMS. Rowad 
addressed the Risk and Opportunities in its main processes to:  
• 
Ensure that the quality Management System can achieve its intended results.  
• 
Enhance the desirable effects in opportunities.  
• 
Prevent, or reduce the undesirable effect of risks  
• 
Achieve improvement in the processes.  
• 
Stronger focus on business continuity & organizational resilience.  
Rowad has integrated and implemented actions to address risk and opportunity into its Quality 
Management System.  
6.1.1 Actions  
Rowad plans actions to address risks and opportunities and evaluate the effectiveness 
of these actions, which are proportionate to the potential impact on the conformity of 
products and services.  
6.2 Quality Objectives   
Rowad establishes the quality objectives to turn broad policy statements into practical, 
measurable actions that drive improvement and customer satisfaction.

6.3 Planning for Changes  
Rowad determines the need for changes to the quality management system. Rowad considers 
the following:  
• 
Purpose of the changes and their potential consequences  
• 
The impact of the changes on the Quality Management System 
• 
Resource availability  
• 
Allocation or reallocation of responsibilities and authorities  
The Request for Document Change Form shall be used to address and manage requests for 
changes. Any changes related to internal or external issues and interested parties shall be 
discussed with the CEO. The impact of changes as well as the plan for change shall be 
prepared by the Quality Assurance manager.  
7. Support   
7.1 Resources  
7.1.1 General  
Rowad determines and provides the resources needed for the establishment, 
implementation, maintenance and continual improvement of the quality management 
system. Rowad consider the following:  
• 
Capabilities for, and constraints on, existing internal resources  
• 
What needs to be obtained from external providers  
• 
Possible software validation for monitoring/measurement tools.  
Rowad determines and provides the resources needed to implement and to maintain the 
quality management system and to continually improve its effectiveness and to enhance 
customer satisfaction by meeting customer requirements.  
  
7.1.2 People  
Rowad determines and provides the necessary people for the effective implementation 
of its quality management system and for the operation and control of its processes. 
Rowad’s Manpower Planning and Talent Acquisition Process is addressed in detailed 
steps. Human Resources Department, along with respective processes in charge, 
ensure that personnel performing work affecting quality are competent and qualified. 
The Talent Development Process addresses the steps for training.

7.1.3 Infrastructure  
Rowad determines, provides and maintains the infrastructure necessary for the 
operation of its processes and to achieve conformity of products and services. Also, 
Rowad expands to include digital infrastructure (remote work platforms, automated 
systems, AI-driven tools, e.g. ERP, Unifier, Cost-OS, Hits, CRM, etc.). The infrastructure 
includes:  
• 
Buildings and associated utilities.  
• 
Equipment, including hardware.  
• 
Transportation resources.  
• 
Information and communication technology.  
7.1.4 Environment for the Operation of Processes  
Rowad determines, provides and maintains the environment necessary for the operation 
of its processes and to achieve conformity of products and services. The environment 
necessary for the operation includes:  
• 
Social  
• 
Psychological  
• 
Physical  
7.1.5 Monitoring & Measuring Resources  
Rowad determines and provides the resources needed to ensure valid and reliable 
results when monitoring or measuring is used to verify the conformity of products and 
services to requirements. Quality Process Control of Measuring Devices defines the steps 
needed to monitor and verify the measuring equipment. Also, Rowad focuses on 
managing digital processes, automation, AI, and data security as part of the QMS.  
  
7.2 Competence  
Rowad assesses the competence of all its personnel based on their education and experience, 
ensuring it meets the standards required to maintain the performance and effectiveness of the 
Quality Management System. Training and development are carried out according to the annual 
training plan, which is designed based on identified staff requirements and needs.  
Rowad, where applicable, acquires and retains the necessary documents/ sources that prove 
competence, and evaluates the effectiveness of these sources; more details are mentioned in the 
“Training and Development” Process.  
7.3 Awareness  
Rowad Modern Engineering ensures that people doing work under its control are aware of:

a) The quality policy which is posted and communicated.  
b) Relevant quality objectives and KPIs.  
c) Their contribution to the effectiveness of the quality management system, including the 
benefits of improved performance, through PDCA cycle across all company’s processes.  
d) Online recorded awareness created for the entire processes.  
e) The implication of not conforming with the quality management system requirements, 
linked with the quality objectives score.  
f) The quality culture and ethical behavior as part of their responsibilities  
7.4 Communication  
ROWAD Modern Engineering determines the internal and external communications relevant to 
the quality management system.  
The control of communication is carried out for external and internal communication and 
addressed in “Control of Documents & Communication” Process.  
  
7.5 Documented Information  
7.5.1 General   
Rowad Modern Engineering quality management system includes:  
a) Documented information required by ISO 9001:2015.   
b) Documented information as determined by Rowad to be necessary for the 
effectiveness of the quality management system.  
Rowad stresses greater attention to managing digitalization, automation, AI, and data 
protection.  
7.5.2 Creating & Updating  
When creating documented information, Rowad ensures appropriate:  
a) Identification and description (e.g. title, date, or reference number).  
b) Format (e.g.  language, software version, graphics) and media.  
c) Review and approval for suitability and adequacy.  
d) Tracking logs.  
7.5.3 Control of Documented Information  
Documented information required by the quality management system and by ISO 
9001:2015, are controlled to ensure:  
a) Availability and suitability for use, where and when it is needed via Rowad e-filing 
system created per project/department.

b) It is adequately protected during the project life cycle and close-out (e.g. from 
loss of confidentiality, improper use, or loss of integrity).  
For the check of documented information, Rowad has addressed the following 
activities, as applicable:  
a) Distribution, access, retrieval and usage (e.g., stamps & distribution matrix)  
b) Storage and preservation, including preservation of legibility in Rowad premises.  
c) Control of changes (e.g. version control).  
d) Retention and disposition.  
   
Documented information of external origin is identified and controlled by Rowad to 
ensure it is necessary for the planning and operation of the quality management 
system.  
Documented information retained as evidence of conformity is protected from unintended 
alterations.  
“Control of Records, Filing, Archiving and Backup Process” details all information 
regarding the documented information.  
8. Operation  
8.1 Operational Planning and Control  
• 
Rowad plans, implements and controls the processes needed to meet the requirements 
for the provision of products and services.  
• 
Rowad manages external providers/suppliers and upstream/downstream lifecycle 
impacts, considering the following:   
o 
Climate change adaptation/mitigation  
o 
Biodiversity protection  
o 
Lifecycle perspective beyond direct operations  
o 
Emergency (e.g., fire, spill, explosion). vs. abnormal operations 
(e.g., process start- 
up/shutdown, maintenance).  
8.2 Requirements for Products and Services  
8.2.1 Customer Communication  
Rowad’s communications with Customers include:

a) Providing information relating to products and services.  
b) Handling inquiries, contracts or orders, including changes.  
c) Obtaining customer feedback relating to products and services, including 
customer complaints and customer satisfaction surveys.  
d) Handling or controlling customer property.  
e) Establishing specific requirements for contingency actions, when relevant.  
  
8.2.2 Determining the requirements for products and services  
When determining the requirements for the products and services to be offered to 
customers, ROWAD Modern Engineering ensures that:  
a) The requirements for the products and services are defined, including: 
I. 
Any applicable statutory and regulatory requirements. 
II. 
Those considered necessary by the organization.  
b) Rowad can meet the demands of the products and services.  
8.2.3 Review of the requirements for products and services  
Rowad ensures that it can meet the requirements for products and services to be 
offered to customers by conducting a review before committing to supplying products 
and services to a customer.  
8.2.4 Changes to requirements for products and services  
ROWAD Modern Engineering ensures that relevant documented information is amended, 
and that relevant people are made aware of the changed requirements when the 
requirements for products and services are changed.  
8.3 Design and development of products and services  
Rowad carries out the check of design for minor issues, and for EPC projects, outsourcing is 
considered for design scope and Rowad team is coordinating with the service providers to 
ensure that client requirements are met. Refer to “Engineering Process”. 
8.4 Control of externally provided processes, products and services  
8.4.1 General  
ROWAD Modern Engineering ensure that externally provided processes, products and 
services conform to requirements of the related activity.  
Rowad determines and applies criteria for the evaluation, selection, monitoring of 
performance, and re-evaluation of external providers, based on their ability to provide 
processes or products and services in accordance with requirements. Rowad retains 
documented information about these activities and any necessary actions arising from

the evaluations. The steps of evaluation are explained in detail in the “Evaluation of 
External Providers Process”.   
8.4.2 Type and extent of control  
Rowad ensures that externally provided processes, products and services do not 
adversely affect Rowad’s ability to consistently deliver conforming products and services 
to its customers.  
8.4.3 Information for External Providers  
Rowad ensures the adequacy of requirements prior to their communication to the external 
provider. The procedures are explained in detail in “Subcontractor Management” 
Process.   
8.5 Production and Service Provision  
8.5.1 Control of Production and Service Provision  
ROWAD modern Engineering implements production and service provision under 
controlled conditions.  
“Control of Production”, “Material Inspection” & “Quality Plan Inspection and Testing” 
Processes define the required procedures to control Rowad output products.  
8.5.2 Identification and Traceability  
ROWAD Modern Engineering uses suitable means to identify its output when it is 
necessary to ensure the conformity of products and services. Rowad identifies the 
status of outputs with respect to monitoring and measuring requirements throughout 
production and service provision. Rowad controls the unique identification of the 
outputs when traceability is a requirement and retains the documented information 
necessary to enable traceability. Process “Control of Documents & Communication” 
explains such procedures along with “Equipment Management” & Control of measuring 
devices Process.  
8.5.3 Property Belonging to Customers or External Providers  
Rowad exercise care with property belonging to customers or external providers while it is 
under Rowad’s control or being used by Rowad through handling & controlling 
customers’ custody following the company process.  
Rowad identifies, verify, protect and safeguard customer’s or external providers’ property 
provided for use or incorporation into the products and services.  
When the property of a customer or external provider is lost, damaged or otherwise 
found to be unsuitable for use, Rowad reports this to the customer or external provider 
and retains documented information on what has occurred. Process “Material Control”

8.5.4 Preservation  
Rowad preserves the outputs during production and service provision, to the extent 
necessary to ensure conformity to requirements.  
8.5.5 Post-delivery Activities  
Rowad meets requirements for post-delivery activities associated with the products and 
services according to DLP warranties.  
In determining the extent of post-delivery activities that are required, Rowad considers:  
a) Statutory and regulatory requirements.  
b) The potential undesired consequences are associated with its products and 
services.   
c) The nature, usage and intended lifetime of its products and services.  
d) Customer requirements and feedback.  
8.5.6 Control of Changes  
Rowad reviews and controls changes for production or service provision, to the extent 
necessary to ensure continuing conformity with requirements.  
Rowad retains documented information describing the results of the review of changes, 
the person(s) authorizing the change, and any necessary actions arising from the review. 
Process “Control of Documents & Communication” explains such procedures.  
8.6 Release of Products and Services  
Rowad implements planned arrangements, at appropriate stages, to verify that the product and 
service requirements have been met. The release of products and services to the customer does 
not occur until the planned arrangements have been satisfactorily completed, unless otherwise 
approved by a relevant authority and, as applicable, by the customer.  
Process “Quality plan Inspection & Testing” & “Control of Production” defines the required 
procedures to release the output products of Rowad.  
8.7 Control of Nonconforming Outputs  
ROWAD Modern Engineering ensures that outputs that do not conform to their requirements are 
identified and controlled to prevent their unintended use or delivery.  
Rowad takes appropriate actions based on the nature of the nonconformity and its effect on the 
conformity of products and services. Process “Control of Non-Conformity” explains such 
procedures.

9. Performance Evaluation  
9.1 Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis and Evaluation  
9.1.1 General   
ROWAD Modern Engineering evaluates continually the performance and the 
effectiveness of the quality management system through quality performance indicators 
(QPI) and key performance indicators (KPI).  
9.1.2 Customer Satisfaction  
ROWAD Modern Engineering monitor customers’ perceptions of the degree to which 
their needs and expectations have been fulfilled via customer satisfaction surveys. 
Rowad determines the methods for obtaining, monitoring and reviewing this information 
with proper analysis and action. Such procedures are explained in “Customer 
Satisfaction” Process  
9.1.3 Analysis and Evaluation  
ROWAD Modern Engineering analyze and evaluate appropriate data and information 
arising from monitoring and measurement.  
The results of analysis are used to evaluate:   
a) Conformity of products and services.  
b) The degree of customer satisfaction.  
c) The performance and effectiveness of the quality management system.   
d) If planning has been implemented effectively.  
e) The effectiveness of actions taken to address risks and opportunities.  
f) The performance of external provider initially & periodically.  
g) The need for improvements to the quality management system.  
9.2 Internal Audit  
Rowad Modern Engineering conducts internal audits at planned intervals to provide information 
and assure that quality management system conforms to Rowad processes and ISO 9001: 2015 
based on the annual audit program & plan.  
All procedures of internal audit are outlined in Process “Internal Audit”.  
 
9.3 Management Review  
9.3.1 General  
Rowad Modern Engineering’s top management conduct an annual review of the Quality 
Management System across all branches and projects to ensure its continued suitability,

10. Improvement  
10.1 General  
ROWAD Modern Engineering identifies and selects opportunities for improvement and 
implements any necessary actions to meet customer requirements and enhance customer 
satisfaction.  
These include:  
a) Improving products and services to meet requirements as well as to address future needs 
and expectations.  
b) Correcting, preventing or reducing undesired effects.  
c) Improving the performance and effectiveness of the quality management system.  
d) Focusing on innovation, stakeholder satisfaction, resilience improvements.  
10.2 Nonconformity and Corrective Action  
When a nonconformity occurs, including any arising from complaints, Rowad takes appropriate 
actions as per process “Control of Non-Conformity” Process.  
10.3 Continual Improvement  
ROWAD Modern Engineering continually improves the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of 
the quality management system.  
Rowad conducts analyses and evaluations, including management reviews and Lessons 
Learned surveys, to identify arising needs or opportunities for continual improvement. Rowad’s 
standard processes “Project Closeout” and “Management Leadership and Commitment” 
describe such procedures.
